propositions: A single pending entry in the queue disables the O(1) fast-path gate marker for the entire store, forcing a full directory walk on every subsequent write until the pending set empties

The current all-or-nothing marker design clears itself whenever any pending entry is found, rather than recording which tickets have live queue entries, causing O(store-size) cost for stores with standing backlogs

The marker should generalize to record a 'live' set of ticket ids with enqueued entries, allowing scoped O(backlog-size) reductions instead of O(store-size) full walks while maintaining TTL-based staleness bounds
Scoped marker probes must never rewrite the marker so the TTL continues to measure from the last full walk, preserving the existing race-safety contract

The scan loop including f400's (not_before_ns, ticket_id) service-order sort must be extracted into a shared helper used by both full-walk and scoped-walk paths to ensure ordering parity and prevent starvation
